newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission will fix annual C-sugar penalty.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission will fix annual C-sugar penalty.

text.p: The latest sugar production estimates will be discussed by the European Union's sugar management committee on Wednesday, an EU official said.
"The Commission has listed an exchange of views on the latest balance sheet for the period October 1, 1995 to September 30, 1996," the official said.
The balance sheet will not be final because several member states, including Britain, are still waiting for the last of their crop production figures to be submitted, the official added.
The European Commission will announce the annual penalty for "C", non-quota, sugar sold on the internal market to the management committee, the official said.
"Non quota, or C sugar has to be sold on the world market and if any is not exported within a year of production it attracts a sizeable penalty," the official added.
A senior Commission official said that the penalty, which is fixed every year, was not expected to be used. "It is an effective encouragement to export," the official said.
The committee will also fix molasses import duties, the official said.
"The committee is due to fix molasses import duties but no significant changes are foreseen," he said.
Duties on imported molasses have remained steady since the beginning of December at the ordinary rate of 0.41 Ecus per 100 kg for cane.
Beet molasses duties have been suspended at zero since early last year.
